INTRODUCTION

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) with its headquarters in Seoul, Republic of Korea, is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. GGGI works with countries around the world, building their capacity and working collaboratively on green growth policies that can impact the lives of millions. The organization partners with countries, multilateral institutions, government bodies, and private sector to help build economies that grow strongly and are more efficient and sustainable in the use of natural resources, less carbon intensive, and more resilient to climate change.

GGGI has a diverse portfolio of programs in developing countries around the world. These in-country programs, together with global products and services, focus on delivering results through an integrated approach of evidence-based green growth planning and implementation aligned to countries’ development priorities. The organization also focuses on knowledge development and management activities which build a strong theoretical and empirical basis for green growth, while providing concrete options and guidance for policymakers; as well as building the conditions for public and private green infrastructure investments. To learn more about GGGI please visit www.gggi.org.

GGGI commenced operations in the Pacific in 2014, and it now has programs and projects in five member countries including Fiji, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea (PNG), Tonga, and Vanuatu, and in three partner countries, Samoa, Solomon Island, and Tuvalu. GGGI works in other Pacific Island Countries (PICs) in the Southern and Northern Pacific through its regional programs. The partnership between GGGI and PICs is built on supporting their transition towards low carbon, environmentally sustainable, climate resilient and socially inclusive economies. In 2025, GGGI has 32 active projects with its total staff expected to grow to 140 by end of 2025. In addition to national country programs, GGGI proactively implements regional programs and projects in the Pacific that benefit two or more countries for logistical reasons and economy of scale aligned with regional best practice.

Rural electrification in the Pacific face’s significant barriers, including geographical challenges due to scattered and remote islands, which make infrastructure development costly and logistically complex. To address this challenge and improve rural electrification access in the Pacific, the European Union (EU) is implementing the Pacific Regional Electrification Program (EU Pac-REP) across all PICs. This EUR 15 million program aims to advance the inclusive, sustainable and resilient socioeconomic development across 13 selected PICs including Cook Islands, Fiji, Papua New Guinea (PNG), Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu, as well as Timor-Leste. The aim is to increase access to electricity in rural and remote areas, reduce carbon emission and reliance on imported fossil fuels.
POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Pacific Regional Implementation Officer, the National Coordination Officer will serve as the principal in-country focal point for the implementation of the EU Pac-REP program in Kiribati. The National Coordination Officer will support the delivery of program activities at the national level by providing technical, coordination, and operational support across renewable energy, rural electrification, and stakeholder engagement activities. The role will work closely with government counterparts, regional stakeholders, development partners, communities, and the GGGI project team to ensure activities are implemented effectively, aligned with national priorities, and delivered in accordance with program objectives and donor requirements. The position also requires regular coordination with regional Pac-REP teams and participation in program reporting, consultations, and knowledge-sharing activities across participating Pacific Island Countries.
PURPOSE

The National Coordination Officer is a in country position that serves as the principal point of coordination between GGGI's Pac-REP program team and the Government of The role is pivotal to the successful delivery of both Pac-REP outcomes at the country’s level, providing sustained, high-quality technical and advisory support across a three-year implementation period.

The National Coordination Officer will be based in Kiribati and will be required to undertake travel to provincial, outer island, and rural communities as required by program activities. The position requires a practitioner who combines strong technical expertise in renewable energy and rural electrification with proven ability to navigate national policy development processes, facilitate multi-stakeholder dialogue and produce high-quality analytical and policy outputs.
ENGAGEMENT

The National Coordination Officer will report to the Pacific Regional Implementation Officer (RIO) and maintain regular reporting and coordination with the Director of the Energy Planning Department (EPD), MISE, who will provide day to day direction on priorities within the endorsed work plan and will be invited to contribute feedback to the Officer’s performance review. The Officer will be based within Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy (MISE) and work closely with EPD to support the delivery of departmental activities, objectives, and outcomes. All annual workplans, activity schedules, and key reports will be prepared in consultation with EPD and submitted to MISE for review and endorsement prior to implementation. These will include a single consolidated GGGI energy work plan and progress updates for Kiribati, covering EU Pac-REP and Renew Pacific/KOIEP and other allocated energy related project by MISE.

The Officer will keep MISE informed of programme progress and ensure that all in-country activities, meetings, consultations, and official travel are coordinated through MISE. The Officer will also participate in relevant MISE meetings and planning processes to ensure that Pac-REP activities are aligned with national energy priorities and government objectives. The National Coordination Officer will also participate in regional Pac-REP coordination meetings and contribute to reporting requirements for the European Union as required, with draft reports shared with EPD before submission. Policy and Cabinet process are led by MISE, which the Officer will support and positions on behalf Government in regional meetings will be agreed with MISE beforehand.

The Officer will work within the Energy Coordination protocol agreed between GGGI and MISE. The Officer will work with all energy personnel supported by GGGI, MISE personnel, so that EPD receives one consolidated GGGI energy work plan and progress update, will receive monthly technical updates from all personnel for that purpose, and will coordinate outer island visits and community consultations with stakeholders and MISE to avoid duplicate consultations.
DELIVERY
The National Coordination Officer will be responsible for but not limited to:

Coordinating with MISE through EPD and in agreement with EPD, with outer government focal points in Kiribati, including Public Utilities Board (PUB), Kiribati Green Energy Solutions and other relevant departments, ensuring effective collaboration and national ownership of program activities.
Maintaining regular engagement with government counterparts, utilities, and key stakeholders in coordination with EPD to support implementation and alignment with national energy priorities.
Supporting the planning, implementation, and monitoring of program activities agreed with MISE, ensuring timely delivery of outputs and achievement of targets.

Undertaking outer island travel as required to support project implementation, site visits, consultations, and monitoring activities, coordinated through MISE and with the GGGI related project focal points
Collaborating with Pac-REP coordinators in Fiji, Solomon Islands, and other participating countries to strengthen regional coordination, peer learning, and exchange of best practices
Supporting regional workshops, technical meetings, and knowledge-sharing activities to promote collaboration and program coherence.
Establishing and maintaining working relationships with regional organizations, development partners, and technical institutions to support coordinated implementation.

Ensuring that relevant data, assessments, and recommendations are integrated into the design and delivery of program activities. Project data, assessment and reports will be shared with EPD and kept in departmental records.

Supporting EPD, which leads sector coordination, in coordinating with EU-funded initiatives and other partner programs in Kiribati’s energy sector to strengthen collaboration and avoid duplication of efforts.

Supporting the preparation of reports, briefing notes, and coordination updates related to program implementation and partner engagement activities. Draft reports and briefing notes will be shared with EPD before submission to the EU or other external parties.

Liaising with the GGGI relate energy project focal points and the GGGI Country Representative so that EPD receives a single consolidated GGGI energy work plan and progress update, and promptly informing EPD of any planned GGGI proposal, concept note, funding request or activity concerning Kiribati energy so that it can be discussed and agreed with MISE before submission or commencement.

Supporting EPD in monitoring the compliance of GGGI support energy activities with the Memorandum of Understanding, the Energy Coordination Protocol, national laws, standards and codes and the work plans endorsed by MISE, and reporting any non-compliance or material risk to EPD in a timely manner.

Mentoring EPD officers as a defined capacity-building and knowledge transfer output of the post, and preparing, before the end of the contract, a handover plan covering documentation, data and records for EPD.
QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
Bachelors in energy engineering, electrical, mechanical, renewable energy, environmental science, public policy, development economics, or a closely related discipline.
A postgraduate and/or Master's qualification in a related field will be considered an advantage.

A minimum of five (5) to eight (8) years of progressive professional experience in the energy sector, with a demonstrable focus on renewable energy, rural electrification, or sustainable energy access in Pacific Island Country or comparable Small Island Developing State (SIDS) contexts.
Proven ability to provide evidence-based technical and policy advice on renewable energy systems, off-grid solutions and rural electrification to government, utilities and communities.
Strong analytical skills in reviewing energy policy, regulatory frameworks and sector strategies, identifying gaps and developing practical reform-oriented recommendations.
Experience supporting preparation and quality assurance of technical and policy documents, including feasibility studies, investment proposals, procurement documents and sector strategies.
Experience working with government counterparts on policy development and consultation processes, including facilitation of stakeholder engagement and technical working groups.
Practical experience supporting renewable energy project implementation, including feasibility work, procurement support, contractor coordination, site supervision and community engagement.
Experience working in rural and outer island contexts with strong interpersonal and cross-cultural communication skills.
Ability to maintain programme records and contribute to monitoring, evaluation, learning and knowledge-sharing outputs.

Experience supporting government advisory work in Kiribati or the Pacific, including engagement with senior officials and Cabinet-level processes and familiarity with formal policy and regulatory procedures in Kiribati.
Track record of supporting or overseeing renewable energy project development, including feasibility assessment, procurement support, contractor supervision and community engagement.
Prior engagement with international organizations, development banks, bilateral donors, or EU-funded programs in the Pacific is a distinct advantage.
Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, with the ability to produce polished policy and technical documents to a professional standard.
Proficiency in local languages relevant to Kiribati is highly advantageous and will be given significant weight in the selection process.
FUNTIONAL
Strong analytical capability, with the ability to synthesize complex policy, technical and financial information into accessible well-structured documents.
Sound knowledge of renewable energy technologies appropriate for rural and off-grid electrification, including solar PV, mini-grids, battery storage and hybrid systems.

Understanding investment planning, project finance and financing mechanisms relevant to rural electrification in the Pacific, including concessional finance, blended finance and community-based models.
Familiarity with climate change policy frameworks, Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and their linkages to national energy planning.
Competency in monitoring and evaluation, including the ability to contribute to program indicator tracking and results reporting aligned with EU GERF standards.

High degree of cultural sensitivity and respect for diversity, with experience working in cross-cultural settings and a deep appreciation for the values and social systems of Pacific Island communities.
High degree of personal organization with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outputs within program timelines.
CORPORATE
Understand and actively support GGGI's mission, vision, and values.
Promote the optimum use of public resources.
Promote an organizational culture of trust, transparency, respect, and partnership.
Process and share information easily.
Manage emotions and stress positively, build rapport, and resolve conflict constructively.
Promote creativity and innovation among staff.
WORK CONDITIONS

This is a G8, national grade level in GGGI's salary scale. Determination of base salary is subject to candidate's experience, academic background and internal equity. GGGI provides 15% of base salary towards retirement plan/long-term savings, 27 days of annual leave, and private health insurance that covers dental and vision.

GGGI is committed to providing a work environment that is sufficiently flexible to accommodate diverse life-cycle challenges and assist Staff members to achieve a better balance between work and personal/family commitments, thus ensuring high performance, long-term productivity, and well-being of Staff members.

Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
